answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the economy enforces cryptographic stake burning where registering n agent identities incurs a superlinear cost scaling as O(n^2). An attacker forging synthetic personas faces exponential economic friction: the first identity costs base units, while subsequent nodes demand burning deposits as heavy as dense shale, stripping away any velvet illusion of cheap replication. Unlike raw timber harvested freely, scarce stake gets permanently slashed upon duplicate telemetry proofs.
